title: Suicide prevention through a SafetyPlan intervention for patients after a suicide attempt or in suicidal crises (SAFETY+)
summary:
Suicidal thoughts and suicidal behavior are a serious social and health problem in Germany. Nevertheless, there is still no standardized treatment program in Germany for people who are at risk of suicide. Our study plans to implement an intervention (SafetyPlan) designed to protect people from suicide or suicide attempts. We want to investigate whether this intervention can reduce the number of suicide attempts within one year after hospitalization. Another point of research interest is whether the intervention can be implemented (in everyday treatment). We would like to investigate the effectiveness of this measure, as this has not yet been done in German psychiatric hospitals. To this end, we are comparing the SafetyPlan intervention with normal inpatient treatment. Participants in the study are randomly assigned to one of two groups (intervention group, control group). In both groups, participants receive the usual treatment and support provided on the ward, which normally includes planning for further treatment on an outpatient basis. Participants in the intervention group will also receive a consultation in which a safety plan (emergency plan) will be drawn up to prepare them for dealing with future (suicidal) crisis situations. Participants in the intervention group will also be contacted by telephone one week and four weeks after their discharge from the clinic to discuss the content of the emergency plan. People assigned to the control group receive the usual treatment provided on the ward as well as additional information about places they can turn to in a crisis. The study is expected to last one year for all participants. The surveys will be conducted at the following five points in time:
1.) After they have been included in the study (personal interview on site)
2.) Before their discharge from the hospital (in-person interview on site)
3.) Six weeks after discharge (telephone interview)
4.) Six months after discharge (telephone interview)
5.) Twelve months after discharge (telephone interview).
The intervention is expected to lead to fewer suicide attempts in the intervention group (compared to the control group) within one year. In addition, the effects on suicidal thoughts and suicide-related issues (e.g. depression and suicidal rumination) will be investigated. Furthermore, the study will examine whether the measure can be used in normal psychiatric care and provide concrete recommendations for its implementation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. inpatient admission to the clinic due to/as a result of a suicide
2. adequate knowledge of German
3. the willingness to participate in the study aftere being fully informed
Exclusion criteria:
1. the lack of capicity to consent
2. lethal prognosis due to a physical illness
3. mental disability/minor aptitude
4. existing diagnosis of dementia (F00-F03, ICD-10)
